What an annual period label means in this result.

v1 receipts are UK results, so the convention is the UK fiscal year: year
Y is the period from 6 April Y to 5 April Y+1. Another convention needs a
new schema version.

x-policyengine-digests.canonicalization: RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme) over the stated value after removing object members whose value is null (array elements are kept). Numbers are IEEE 754 doubles; integers must lie within +/-(2**53 - 1).
x-policyengine-digests.execution_identity_sha256: {schema_version, country_id, wrapper, model, core, data, certification_status, certificate?} where certificate keeps only bundle_version, country_id, certificate_sha256, compatibility_basis, certified_for_model_version, certified_for_core_version, certified_dataset_sha256 and certified_by
x-policyengine-digests.outputs_sha256: the canonical output payload the receipt binds
x-policyengine-digests.receipt_sha256: the whole receipt without runtime and without reform.name and baseline.name
x-policyengine-digests.reform.reform_sha256: RFC 8785 over {representation, payload} where payload is the reform exactly as given in that representation, nulls kept (a null in a reform can mean something, unlike an absent receipt field)

x-policyengine-rules: years is sorted ascending with no duplicates, and each year is written as an integer (2027, not 2027.0).

supported_years is sorted ascending with no duplicates. A year in years that is not in supported_years is unsupported: the model does not project the dataset to it, so a consumer must show its results as provisional or not at all.
certification_status certified requires certificate; uncertified forbids it.
reform/baseline kind current_law has no representation or reform_sha256 and binding content; kind reform has both.
wheel_sha256 and wheel_sha256_evidence are present together or not at all.

A consumer trusts a certificate only after checking it against the data_releases.<country_id> record of the published policyengine manifest for certificate.bundle_version (verify_certificate()): certificate_sha256 is that record's digest, every other member of certificate except certificate_source, qualification_receipt_sha256 and tro_composition_fingerprint equals what the record states, and data equals the data identity the record determines. certificate_source is the producer's statement and proves nothing.
